page: Microsoft Azure M16-4ms is a specialized memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8280M processor. Hardware provisioning includes 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, 38 MB of shared L3 cache, and 438.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes an atypical memory-to-vCPU distribution exceeding 109 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is not present, with zero GPUs bundled, but the instance incorporates 550 GB of local SSD temporary storage.

Benchmark evaluations reveal that processing throughput is deliberately limited by the low core count. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 884.0 and a multi-core score of 1961.0, accompanied by a PassMark CPU score of 3304.67 and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 2722.46. Memory subsystems demonstrate 151.48 GB/sec in cached small-block read operations, though uncached large-block transfers drop to 18.75 GB/sec read and 15.92 GB/sec write. In-memory data access patterns yield 2.69 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 3.12 GB/sec.

The primary resource tradeoff of the M16-4ms centers on its extreme memory allocation juxtaposed with constrained compute capability. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the configuration offers an advantageous ratio for enterprise software architectures licensed on a per-core basis that strictly require vast memory reserves. Workloads demanding parallel mathematical operations or sustained high CPU throughput will experience resource bottlenecks. The instance is functionally aligned with large in-memory caches, memory-resident database test nodes, and data lookup tiers that prioritize RAM capacity over execution speed.
description: Microsoft Azure M16-4ms is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive workloads with constrained CPU footprint requirements. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor operating at 2.7 GHz, the instance allocates 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, supported by 38 MB of L3 cache and 438 GB of RAM. This configuration yields an extreme ratio of 109.38 GB of memory per core. Bundled with 550 GB of local SSD storage and zero GPU accelerators, it provides local scratch space alongside substantial memory capacity. Benchmark results indicate modest processing capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1961.0, PassMark CPU score of 3304.67, and uncached memory read bandwidth of 18.75 GB/sec, reflecting bottom-tier throughput relative to larger multi-core instances. Cost efficiency is optimized for software licensed on a per-core basis that requires massive RAM capacity. It is primarily fitted for in-memory caching, large dataset staging, and memory-bound databases.
